quotes.speaker: Taylor Jenkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Taylor Jenkins on managing preseason minutes and rotation
quotes.excerpt: nothing set in stone yet, I think it's going to be evolving over the first couple of weeks
quotes.quote: I would say working backwards, I doubt everyone gets to regular season minutes against Indiana. Honestly, really sorting through a lot of stuff right now. So, guys that were out could be in the rotation, could have guys from last night be in the rotation. It's going to be competitive Friday night, it's going to be competitive the first week of the season. Nothing set in stone yet, I think it's going to be evolving over the first couple of weeks right now.
quotes.social_post: Taylor Jenkins says nothing is set in stone for the Grizzlies rotation yet. He expects the lineup to be evolving over the first couple of weeks of the season as they sort through competition for minutes.

quotes.speaker: Taylor Jenkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Taylor Jenkins on balancing player workloads during the preseason
quotes.excerpt: I want to give guys ample sample size to try to build up to a workload
quotes.quote: I could limit minutes, but I want to give guys ample sample size to try to build up to a workload. If my expectation is everyone can play 20 to 25 minutes every single night, we got to be living in that world in three weeks of the preseason. With a lot of depth and trying to see combinations, we're not going to be able to sort through everything just in three weeks with this group. I was trying to be intentional about, hey, if I have certain guys that are going to be out, they're going to get their opportunity the next game.
quotes.social_post: Taylor Jenkins admits that with the current depth of the roster, three weeks of preseason is not enough time to sort through every possible lineup combination.

quotes.speaker: Taylor Jenkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Taylor Jenkins on developing players against defensive pressure
quotes.excerpt: we're going to face pressure regardless of who it's going to be
quotes.quote: We're going to face pressure regardless of who it's going to be. All of our guys have to develop against that style of defense. When you talk about Ryan, Scoot, Gary, you've got Braden, Cas, you even throw Cam in there, you got Tyler, it's going to be different ways that we're going to have to attack pressure. Learning their tendencies, if it's their ability to break down the defense one-on-one, it's playing off of get actions, which we call snap, it's single pick-and-rolls, double pick-and-rolls, it's north-south, east-west, trying to get a feel for one or running habits in our initial shape, which is still a work in progress.
quotes.social_post: Taylor Jenkins says the Grizzlies are focused on teaching their young guards how to attack defensive pressure, noting that their offensive habits are still a work in progress.

quotes.speaker: Taylor Jenkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Taylor Jenkins on building team chemistry and cognitive synergy
quotes.excerpt: they actually have a cognitive kind of synergy with their teammates
quotes.quote: That's the depths of the layers when you talk about chemistry. We can just say chemistry, but what does that mean? Guys vibe with each other and they actually have a cognitive kind of synergy with their teammates. The guy with the ball knows where his teammates are and they know how they're going to be moving or that's maybe that's not the space to go capture based off of how the defense is being deployed. But then vice versa, if I'm off the ball, I know I'm coming into a screen, I know I'm cutting off the ball. That's the stuff that we're trying to wire right now. We are making progress.
quotes.social_post: Taylor Jenkins on team chemistry: It is about having a cognitive synergy where players know exactly where their teammates are and how they are going to move on the floor.
